title: Mosque of Ibn Tulun
summary: The Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun in Cairo was built in 876-879 AD in the style of Samarra, of red brick, around a large court. UNESCO notes its spiral minaret; the IRCICA inventory says the minaret was added in the late 13th century.

uncertainty.note: Construction years given by UNESCO (876-879 AD) and IRCICA (Year of Construction 876-879).

as_recorded.value: the mosque of Ahmed ibn Tulun (876-879 AD)

where.modern_name: Mosque of Ibn Tulun, Cairo, Egypt
where.historical_name: Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun at al-Qata'i, Tulunid Egypt (Abbasid Caliphate)

importance.justification: One of the oldest surviving mosques in Cairo, inside the UNESCO-listed Historic Cairo.

reviewer_note: No model: no heritage, government, museum or scholarly page that I opened gives the minaret height (the figures seen in search are travel pages). IRCICA gives a plan of 47 x 37 m, which conflicts with larger figures elsewhere, so I did not use it. Pin is IRCICA 30 1 43.63 N, 31 14 58.26 E converted.
